name: AgenStart
tagline: A local-first Windows desktop setup assistant that inspects the device, recommends appropriate apps and routes reviewed choices through trusted providers.
problem: New PCs require repetitive checks and installer choices, while automated scripts can silently install untrusted packages without explaining risks or failure modes.
scenario: A Windows user reviews local machine capabilities, selects use cases, chooses from explained software recommendations and explicitly approves a WinGet-backed installation.
differentiation: The user controls every installation, with an inventory- and profile-aware recommendation model and auditable status instead of a cloud-required silent provisioning script.
architecture: Windows inventory and installed software -> profiles/recommendations -> explicit user review -> WinGet/provider adapters -> local progress, diagnostics and setup report.
limitations: An installer cannot universally be rolled back, and not every Windows provider has identical retry guarantees. The README's roadmap is not equivalent to every feature being released.
